record.paper_title: Some open problems in Banach space theory
record.original_question: Let X be an infinite-dimensional Banach space. Does X contain an infinite-dimensional subspace with an unconditional basis?

evidence.quote:
(Q.10) Let X be an infinite-dimensional Banach space. Does X have an infinite-
dimensional subspace with an unconditional basis.?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be an infinite-dimensional (real or complex) Banach space. A sequence $(x_n)_{n=1}^{\infty}$ in a Banach space is called a Schauder basic sequence if every vector in its closed linear span has a unique expansion as a norm-convergent series $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n x_n$. Such a basic sequence is called unconditional if there exists a constant $C \geq 1$ such that for every finitely supported scalar sequence $(a_n)$ and every choice of signs $(\varepsilon_n) \in \{-1,+1\}^{\mathbb{N}}$,
$$\Big\| \sum_n \varepsilon_n a_n x_n \Big\| \leq C \Big\| \sum_n a_n x_n \Big\|.$$
Equivalently, an infinite-dimensional closed subspace $Y \subseteq X$ is said to have an unconditional basis if it admits a Schauder basis that is unconditional.

Question: Must every infinite-dimensional Banach space $X$ contain an infinite-dimensional closed subspace with an unconditional basis?
artifact.status_search_result: Solved negatively by W. T. Gowers and B. Maurey (J. Amer. Math. Soc. 6 (1993), 851–874), who constructed an infinite-dimensional Banach space containing no infinite unconditional basic sequence (in fact, a hereditarily indecomposable space).

status_evidence.title: The unconditional basic sequence problem (Gowers–Maurey)
status_evidence.snippet: Gowers and Maurey construct a Banach space which does not contain any infinite unconditional basic sequence.
status_evidence.claim: The problem was answered in the negative.

status_evidence.title: The Unconditional Basic Sequence Problem (JSTOR)
status_evidence.snippet: J. Amer. Math. Soc. 6 (1993), 851–874, by W. T. Gowers and B. Maurey.
status_evidence.claim: Published solution showing not every infinite-dimensional Banach space has a subspace with an unconditional basis.
